title: Country Calling Codes
description: 254 entries from Google's libphonenumber metadata — 245 countries and territories with an ISO 3166-1 code plus 9 non-geographical codes (+800, +808, +870, +878, +881, +882, +883, +888, +979) — each with its calling code, trunk prefix, international prefix and a valid example number.

id.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, or 001-<code> for a non-geographical service

iso2.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, 001 for the non-geographical services

name.description: English short name from CLDR; non-geographical services are labelled as such

callingCode.description: Calling code with the plus sign

internationalPrefix.description: What you dial before a foreign number from inside the country; null for the nine non-geographical codes

preferredInternationalPrefix.description: Preferred alternative where the metadata gives one

nationalPrefix.description: Trunk prefix for national dialling; null when not declared

nationalPrefixForParsing.description: Pattern libphonenumber uses to strip the prefix when parsing

exampleNumber.description: A valid national number, digits only, unformatted

exampleNumberKind.description: Which number type the example belongs to

mobileNumberPortableRegion.description: True when the metadata flags the country as supporting mobile number portability
